sections.body: Citation mapping and discovery uses machine learning to turn a research literature into a navigable structure. In practice, language models embed paper abstracts and full texts into vector spaces, graph algorithms trace citation links, and clustering methods group papers by shared meaning. The work here is descriptive, not prescriptive: it shows which papers cite which, how clusters form, and where a field is moving. The site's library of 135 research papers and 10,767 extracted claims is the raw material for these maps. Every link points to the original paper, not to a search aggregator.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The state of the field is uneven. Building citation graphs over time is solved in the sense that tools can reliably extract and display links, but interpreting those graphs remains hard because citation practices vary by discipline and decade. Clustering papers by meaning works well for broad topics, yet it often misses subtle differences, novel terminology, or papers that bridge two clusters. Classifying how a paper is cited, whether as support, contrast, or background, is still noisy and cannot fully capture author intent. Bridge studies between fields are promising but prone to false positives, since shared vocabulary does not always mean shared method. Forecasting research trends is the least reliable part, as models can extrapolate recent growth but cannot predict a genuine breakthrough.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader would start with Citation Graphs Over Time to see the backbone of a field and how influence moves across years. Clustering Papers by Meaning then groups those papers by what they actually say, which helps when a citation graph is too dense to read. How a Paper Is Cited zooms in on individual links and explains whether a citation supports, criticizes, or merely mentions the earlier work. Bridge Studies Between Fields uses those citation contexts and clusters to find papers that connect otherwise separate research areas. Forecasting Research Trends takes the patterns from the previous pages and projects them forward, with the caveat that these projections are exploratory rather than certain.
